start_here: Say to your AI: "Publish the engine release for the tip of main again on my builder, using /etc/engine-releases/publish.json." It runs publish on the builder with the repository token on descriptor 3 and tells you the sequence, target and url.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads the publish config the builder install wrote and adds one signed entry to the release feed folder on the builder.
instructions: 1. Have a builder first: run tool:install-an-engine-builder once for the machine. It writes /etc/engine-releases/publish.json, makes the signing key and starts the receiver, which runs publish on every push to the branch, so a hand run is only for publishing again.
2. On the builder, as its builder user, from the tool folder install made (/opt/engine-releases/tool), hand the repository token on descriptor 3 from the vault, never in argv or a file.

3. Run: node tools/publish-an-engine-release/do-work/publish-an-engine-release.mjs publish /etc/engine-releases/publish.json. Add --commit <commit> after the request file to publish an earlier commit the feed holds nothing newer than.

4. Read the one JSON line: commit, sequence (the commit time in seconds), target, url, content (1f: and the BLAKE3 of the tar.gz), bytes, urgent, signature, public_key, already_published, dropped and releases_held. The same commit again answers already_published true and changes nothing.

5. A commit older than the feed's newest for the same target is refused before any build with {"error": "..."} and exit 3 (expected, nothing changed). Run tool:read-an-engine-builder to see the feed afterwards.

worked_examples.title: Publish the third commit of a made-up repository
worked_examples.ask: Publish the engine release for the tip of main on my builder.
worked_examples.given: From tools/publish-an-engine-release/test/publish-an-engine-release.test.mjs (the first publish test, with a fake cargo and rustc): a made-up repository whose branch main has 3 commits made at seconds 1800000001, 1800000002 and 1800000003, the third with the trailer "Release-Urgent: true", and a publish config for base_url https://releases.example.com/engine-releases/. The AI runs on the builder: node tools/publish-an-engine-release/do-work/publish-an-engine-release.mjs publish /etc/engine-releases/publish.json  (token on descriptor 3).
worked_examples.hands_back: {"commit":"<the 40-hex id of the third commit>","sequence":1800000003,"target":"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu","url":"https://releases.example.com/engine-releases/<commit>/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz","content":"1f:<64 hex, the BLAKE3 of the tar.gz>","bytes":<the tar.gz size>,"urgent":true,"signature":"<128 hex>","public_key":"<64 hex of the builder's key>","already_published":false,"dropped":0,"releases_held":<the entries now in feed.json>}; the tar.gz holds trillion-local, product/bin/trillion-mcp-forwarder and the repository's product/ folder, and the entry verifies with the printed public_key. Run again for the same commit it answers already_published true and writes nothing.
